home.headline: Selling into Germany? Three obligations already apply. We show you the ==evidence==.
home.lede:
If you ship to German consumers these obligations apply to you, whether or not you have a company here — accessibility since 28 June 2025, product safety since 13 December 2024, and packaging since before your first parcel.

We check all three against your actual website and send a three-page report with the evidence behind every finding.

obligations.heading: Accessible Online Shop
obligations.text:
Your shop, checkout and customer account have to be usable by people with disabilities, measured against {de|EN 301 549}, and you need a published accessibility statement. The exemption is under 10 staff and under €2m turnover.

Since January 2026 the German market surveillance authority has been running its own checks, not only responding to complaints.

obligations.heading: GPSR Product-Offer Information
obligations.law: General Product Safety Regulation (EU) 2023/988, Article 19 — applies since 13 December 2024
obligations.text:
Every online offer has to show the manufacturer's name, postal address and electronic address.

Only where the manufacturer is not established in the EU must the offer additionally name the responsible person in the Union — an EU manufacturer is that operator itself.

obligations.heading: Registered Packaging
obligations.law: {de|Verpackungsgesetz} — {de|LUCID} registration, required before your first shipment
obligations.text:
Every box, filler and label you send into Germany has to be registered in the {de|LUCID} register and licensed with a dual system. Registration is required _before_ the first shipment.

Marketplaces are obliged to block sellers who have not done it.

home.evidenceIntro: Three findings from a real scan, shown the way the report shows them: the failing element itself, the rule it breaks, and how many instances we counted. The shop is **Nordlicht Home** — we invented it, so nobody’s real findings are on this page.

evidence.heading: Images without alternative text
evidence.text: Images with no alt attribute, so the catalogue is unusable with a screen reader.

evidence.heading: Buttons with no accessible name
evidence.text: Buttons announced only as "button", usually where an icon replaced the text.

evidence.heading: Text contrast below the required ratio
evidence.text: Text below the 4.5:1 contrast minimum, normally a few palette values repeated site-wide.

home.evidenceNote: Automated testing finds a minority of accessibility barriers. These counts are what a machine can prove; they are a floor, not a total. [See the whole report](/sample-report).

comparison.heading: Why not just ask an AI?
comparison.intro: You can, and it will tell you something. Here is what it will not do.
comparison.colAi: An AI or a free scanner

rows.us: Tested with axe-core against WCAG 2.2 AA and {de|EN 301 549}, then checked by hand with a keyboard and a screen reader — which is where most real barriers show up.
rows.ai: Finds only what a machine can detect, and reports that as the whole picture.

rows.us: We search the German {de|LUCID} register under your legal entity and tell you the date we searched.
rows.ai: Cannot see the register at all.

rows.us: We look on the pages the details have to appear on — including a product page, not a category listing — and tell you what was there.
rows.ai: Reads the requirement. Does not open your product pages.

rows.us: A screenshot of the failing element on your own page, the clause it breaks, and the date — a document you can hand to a developer or an authority.
rows.ai: A list of suggestions with nothing behind them.

rows.us: We never tell you that you are compliant. We tell you what the requirement is and what we found. The report generator refuses to print the word.

legal.title: Privacy policy
legal.metaDescription: What personal data Elbebridge collects, why, on what legal basis, and what rights you have under the GDPR.
legal.intro: How we handle personal data under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Last updated 15 August 2026.

blocks.text: The controller for the processing described here is:

This website sets no cookies, embeds no third-party scripts and runs no analytics. Nothing about your visit is used to profile you or to advertise to you. That is why you are not being asked to accept anything.

items.desc: Your email address and whatever you choose to put in the message — normally a store URL and a company name.
To run the requested check and reply to you with the result.
Article 6(1)(b) GDPR — steps taken at your request before entering into a contract.
There is no form and no form provider. Your message goes straight to our mailbox, which is hosted by Google Workspace (Google Ireland Limited) as our processor under a data processing agreement.
Twelve months after our last contact, unless you become a client, in which case statutory retention periods for business correspondence apply.

This site is hosted on GitHub Pages, operated by GitHub, Inc. Their servers record standard access log data: IP address, date and time, the page requested, and the browser identifier your browser sends. We have no access to those logs and build no profile from them.
To deliver the site and to keep it secure and available.
Article 6(1)(f) GDPR — our legitimate interest in operating a secure website.
Retention is governed by GitHub's own privacy statement, which you can read at [docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement).

sections.heading: 5. What we look at when we scan a website

blocks.text: Our scan reads publicly available pages of the website you ask us to check. We record company identification only — the legal entity, its registered address and its registration numbers, as published in that site's own legal notice. We do not log in, we do not place orders, we do not access anything behind authentication, and we do not collect details of named individuals. Our scanner respects robots.txt, identifies itself in its user agent, and makes at most one request per second.

Two of our processors are reachable from the United States. GitHub, Inc. hosts this website and is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; it also offers Standard Contractual Clauses. Google Workspace is contracted through Google Ireland Limited, with the same frameworks in place for any onward transfer. We tell you this rather than claiming everything stays in Europe, because it does not.
Under the GDPR you have the right to:

items: access the personal data we hold about you (Article 15);
receive it in a portable format (Article 20);
object to processing based on legitimate interest (Article 21).

blocks.text: To exercise any of these, write to [hallo@elbebridge.com](mailto:hallo@elbebridge.com). You do not need to give a reason and it costs you nothing.

You can complain to a data protection supervisory authority. The competent authority for us is the {de|Hamburgische Beauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit} (Hamburg Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information).
If we change how we handle data, we update this page and the date at the top. We keep previous versions on file.

legal.title: Accessibility statement
legal.metaDescription: How accessible this website is, how we tested it, and how to tell us if something does not work for you.
legal.intro: We ask other companies about their accessibility statement, so here is ours. This statement covers the website at elbebridge.com and was last reviewed on 15 August 2026.

blocks.text: We believe this site conforms to {de|EN 301 549} and the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2 at level AA. Specifically:

items: every page works with the keyboard alone, and the focus indicator is always visible;
the site ships no JavaScript at all, so nothing depends on scripts loading;
text contrast exceeds the required ratio, and nothing is signalled by colour alone;
text can be resized to 200% without loss of content or horizontal scrolling;
the page structure uses real headings and landmarks, in order;
German terms inside English sentences carry their own language attribute, so a screen reader pronounces them correctly.

blocks.text: Automated testing with axe-core against the WCAG 2.2 AA and {de|EN 301 549} rule sets — the same scan we run for clients — followed by manual testing: keyboard-only navigation with the mouse unplugged, and a screen reader pass with NVDA.

Automated tools detect only a minority of accessibility problems. We say this on our own statement for the same reason we say it in every report we write: a clean automated scan is not a claim of accessibility.
None currently recorded. If we become aware of a barrier we cannot fix immediately, we will list it here with a date by which we expect to fix it.

sections.heading: Tell us if something does not work

blocks.text: If you find a barrier on this site, email [hallo@elbebridge.com](mailto:hallo@elbebridge.com) and tell us what you were trying to do. We reply within five working days. If you need information from this site in a different format, ask and we will send it.

If you are not satisfied with our response, you can contact the German market surveillance authority for the accessibility of products and services ({de|Marktüberwachungsstelle der Länder für die Barrierefreiheit von Produkten und Dienstleistungen}).

legal.title: About our crawler
legal.metaDescription: ElbeBridgeComplianceBot: who runs it, what it requests, how to recognise it in your logs, and how to block it if you would rather we did not look.
legal.intro: Our user agent points at this page, so that anyone who finds it in their logs can tell in one click who we are and what we were doing.

blocks.text: Elbebridge GbR, Hamburg. We check public websites against three German market obligations and sell the findings to the site owner. Write to [hallo@elbebridge.com](mailto:hallo@elbebridge.com) with any question about a request you have seen.
The crawler identifies itself, always, with a contactable address:
`Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; ElbeBridgeComplianceBot/1.0; +https://elbebridge.com/scanner)`
It is a real browser engine rather than a plain HTTP client, because an online shop that renders its catalogue in the browser cannot be checked any other way.
A handful of pages per site, once:

items: one product page, reached from the home page or from a category listing;
the pages that carry your company details — {de|Impressum}, legal notice, terms, privacy or about;
your accessibility statement, if one is linked.

blocks.text: It never submits a form, never signs in, never adds to a basket, and never places an order.

One request per second to any one host, at most, with no more than a handful of hosts in flight at a time. A whole site is usually finished inside a minute. We do not re-scan a site we have already read unless something has changed or the owner asks us to.
We read robots.txt on every request and honour it. To keep us out entirely, add these two lines:
`User-agent: ElbeBridgeComplianceBot`
`Disallow: /`
A disallowed site is recorded as skipped and nothing further is requested. If you would rather tell us directly, email us and we will remove the domain from the list.

What a visitor to your site could see: the page text we read, a screenshot of the pages we tested, the accessibility findings, and the company details you publish. We do not collect personal data about your customers, and we do not sell what we find to anyone but you. See our [privacy policy](/privacy) for the detail.
